newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says wise men back government reform efforts.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says wise men back government reform efforts.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Friday the latest report by the "wise men" panel of independent economic advisors vindicated government efforts to push through reforms.
"The study shows the economic policies of the government are the only viable way towards the sustained improvement of growth and employment in Germany," Rexrodt said in a statement.
"It refutes repeated claims that the government's growth and jobs plan is an attack on the welfare state," he added.

In its report, the five-man panel said the economy would grow 2.5 percent next year after 1.5 percent in 1996, and, although inflation will remain low at 1.75 percent, German unemployment will remain stuck at over four million.

It added that Germany will miss its goal of qualifying for European monetary union, because its budget deficit will fall in 1997 only to 3.3 percent of gross domestic product from an expected 4.2 percent this year.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel, whose budget cleared the parliamentary committee stage on Thursday, wants to get the deficit below the Maastricht treaty ceiling of three percent.
Rexrodt said that the panel supported decisive efforts to cut the budget deficit, reduce taxes and cut state spending as a proportion of total economic output.
Although the consolidation will temporarily dampen demand in the economy, the risks of taking no action are greater, Rexrodt said, agreeing with the panel's conclusions.

Waigel is trying to negotiate a stability pact with other European states to ensure fiscal discipline under the single currency, and Rexrodt said a similar deal between the German federal government, states and local governments was needed.
